Depends on: 2.2.\n- 2.3.1 A portal change with at least one applied field → upsert the record's single `pending`\n  outbox row, merging the field list.\n- 2.3.2 A Salesforce change → never an outbox row.\n- 2.3.3 A portal create → an outbox row with `operation=create`.\n\n**Done when:**\n- a webhook write creates 0 outbox rows;\n- 3 portal edits to one record leave 1 pending row with the union of fields;\n- the edit and its outbox row commit together, or neither does.\n\n### 2.4 Concurrency\nOwner: Ross. Depends on: 2.3.\n- 2.4.1 Transactional test: two threads apply changes to the same record, and the final state\n  and history are correct.\n- 2.4.2 Two whole-record webhooks for one record at the same time: no lost field.\n\n**Done when:** both tests pass reliably (10 runs in a row).\n\n---\n\n## Phase 3: Inbound webhook (path A)\n\n**Goal:** Salesforce changes land in Postgres through the endpoint in `openapi.yml`.\n**Exit:** contract tests for the webhook pass.\n\n### 3.1 Webhook serializer and view\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 2.3, 1.2.\n- 3.1.1 `WebhookEventSerializer`: required fields, `objectType` enum, ISO `occurredAt`; fields\n  outside the brief's scope are ignored.\n- 3.1.2 A `CreateAPIView` that overrides `create` to call `apply()` and answer **200** with\n  `WebhookResult`.\n- 3.1.3 Permission: `IsSalesforceIntegration` with `TokenAuthentication` first, so a bad token\n  gets 401.\n- 3.1.4 A contact webhook whose `customer` isn't known yet: store `customer_salesforce_id`.\n  When the customer arrives, link waiting contacts.\n\n**Done when:**\n- 401 without a token, 403 with a portal user's token, 400 on a malformed payload, and\n  nothing stored in any of those cases;\n- 200 with `applied`, `duplicate`, `echo`, `superseded` or `no_change` in the right cases;\n- the brief's sample payload works.\n\n### 3.2 Dedupe retention\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 3.1.\n- 3.2.1 A daily dramatiq-crontab job deletes `ChangeEvent` rows older than 7 days.\n\n**Done when:** a test with an injected clock shows an 8-day-old row removed and a 6-day-old row\nkept.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 4: Fake Salesforce\n\n**Goal:** a separate process that behaves like the parts of Salesforce we depend on, and that\ncan be broken on demand.\n**Exit:** the fake runs in compose, and each mode is tested.\n\n### 4.1 The fake app and its process\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 1.1.2.\n- 4.1.1 `fake_salesforce` app with its own settings module and SQLite database.\n- 4.1.2 A compose service `fake-salesforce` (same image) on port 8001.\n- 4.1.3 Record API: upsert by external ID, update by ID, and a \"changed since T\" query paged at\n  2,000 records (Q3, Q13). Token-checked.\n\n**Done when:** an upsert twice with the same external ID gives one record, and the query pages\ncorrectly.\n\n### 4.2 Failure modes\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 4.1.\n- 4.2.1 Control endpoint: `up`, `slow` (delay), `throttle` (429 with `Retry-After`), `error`\n  (5xx), `reject` (400 for a given record).\n- 4.2.2 \"Down\" is a stopped container: `docker compose stop fake-salesforce`.\n\n**Done when:** each mode returns the documented response.\n\n### 4.3 Webhook sender\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 4.1, 3.1.\n- 4.3.1 A record change in the fake (a \"sales edit\" via its control endpoint, or our API write)\n  sends a whole-record webhook to the portal with `eventId`, `occurredAt` and `changedBy`. Our\n  own writes are sent with `changedBy` = the integration user (the echo).\n- 4.3.2 A control option to send the same webhook twice, or an older one after a newer one.\n\n**Done when:** a sales edit in the fake appears in the portal within 30 s.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 5: Outbound (path B) and the outage\n\n**Goal:** portal edits reach Salesforce under the cap, and survive outages and restarts.\n**Exit:** a restart while the fake is down loses nothing, and the measured rate never exceeds\nthe configured cap.\n\n### 5.1 `SalesforceClient`\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 1.2, 4.1.\n- 5.1.1 An `httpx` client: `upsert(object_type, external_id, fields)` and `update(...)`.\n- 5.1.2 Maps responses to outcomes: ok, unreachable, throttled (with `Retry-After`), rejected,\n  auth failure.\n- 5.1.3 An in-process fake for unit tests, with the same outcomes.\n\n**Done when:** each outcome is mapped correctly against the in-process fake.\n\n### 5.2 Shared rate limiter\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 5.1.\n- 5.2.1 A Redis token bucket (Lua, atomic) at `SALESFORCE_RATE_LIMIT`, shared by every worker\n  thread and process, and used for sends, retries, probes and catch-up queries.\n- 5.2.2 On a 429: pause until `Retry-After`, halve the rate, then add 5 req/s every 30 s back\n  up to the limit.\n\n**Done when:** with the limit at 5 req/s and an injected clock, 100 calls take ≥ 19 s (no\nwindow exceeds the limit); a 429 halves the rate.\n\n### 5.3 Outbound task\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 5.2, 2.3.\n- 5.3.1 A Dramatiq actor with `max_retries=0` that claims due rows (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`,\n  `lease_until`), reads the record's **current** values for the fields, and sends.\n- 5.3.2 Outcome handling per design §6: `sent` and store the Salesforce ID; backoff\n  1/2/4/8… s capped at 60 s; 429 → slow the limiter down; 400 → `needs_review`; 401/403 →\n  stop and alert.\n- 5.3.3 Wake-up: a Redis nudge on commit (`transaction.on_commit`), plus a 5-second crontab\n  sweep.\n\n**Done when:**\n- a portal edit is in the fake within 30 s;\n- a 5xx is retried and then sent;\n- a 400 goes to `needs_review` and is never dropped;\n- a worker killed mid-call loses its lease and the row is sent again.\n\n### 5.4 Down detection and probe\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 5.3.\n- 5.4.1 After 5 consecutive unreachable failures, `SyncState` says `down` and sending stops.\n- 5.4.2 A probe every 10 s. On success: `up`, trigger catch-up (phase 6), then make every\n  pending row due.\n\n**Done when:** with the fake stopped, the state goes `down` after 5 failures; with it\nrestarted, it goes `up` within 10 s and the drain starts.\n\n### 5.5 Restart-while-down test (brief check)\nOwner: Ross. Depends on: 5.4.\n- 5.5.1 Stop the fake, make portal edits, restart the worker container, start the fake again,\n  and check every edit arrives in the fake.\n\n**Done when:** that test passes. This is one of the brief's four demo checks.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 6: Catch-up (path C)\n\n**Goal:** Salesforce changes made during an outage aren't lost.\n**Exit:** edits made in the fake while webhooks are switched off reach the portal after\nrecovery.\n\n### 6.1 Catch-up task\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 5.4, 4.1.\n- 6.1.1 Query \"changed since watermark − overlap\", 2,000 per page, through the limiter.\n- 6.1.2 Each record goes to `apply()` as a Salesforce change: `event_id` = record ID +\n  modified time, with a **field-level** echo check.\n- 6.1.3 Advance the watermark only after a page commits.\n- 6.1.4 Schedules: on recovery (before the drain), and every 5 minutes (crontab).\n\n**Done when:**\n- with webhooks off in the fake, 3 sales edits are in the portal after catch-up;\n- a second run changes nothing (idempotent);\n- catch-up runs before the drain.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 7: Portal API\n\n**Goal:** the endpoints in `openapi.yml` work, as thin generic views over `apply()`.\n**Exit:** contract tests per endpoint pass, and the responses match `openapi.yml`.\n\n### 7.1 Customers and contacts\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 2.3, 1.2.\n- 7.1.1 Serializers with explicit fields and camelCase names (as in `openapi.yml`).\n- 7.1.2 `ListCreateAPIView` with cursor pagination and the filters in the contract.\n- 7.1.3 `RetrieveUpdateAPIView`, PATCH only, with `perform_create` / `perform_update` calling\n  `apply()`.\n\n**Done when:**\n- 201/200/400/401/404 as in the contract;\n- a list with 50 rows has a fixed query count;\n- a PATCH writes a history row and an outbox row.\n\n### 7.2 History endpoints\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 7.1.\n- 7.2.1 A `ListAPIView` over `FieldChange`, newest first, with the `?field=` filter.\n\n**Done when:** the brief's \"who changed the phone, who changed the city\" can be answered from\nthe API, including a superseded row.\n\n### 7.3 Sync status endpoint\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 5.4.\n- 7.3.1 A `RetrieveAPIView` (staff only) returning `SyncStatus`: up/down, pending count, oldest\n  pending age, needs-review count, portal edits/s, limiter rate, last catch-up time.\n\n**Done when:** the values match the database in a test, and a non-staff user gets 403.\n\n### 7.4 Generated schema check\nOwner: Ross. Depends on: 7.1–7.3.\n- 7.4.1 Generate the schema from the code (`drf-spectacular`) and compare it with\n  `docs/openapi.yml`. Any difference is fixed in the code or the contract.\n\n**Done when:** no unexplained differences.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 8: Demo and end-to-end check\n\n**Goal:** one command from a fresh checkout shows the brief's four checks, with a cap low\nenough to see.\n**Exit:** `bash scripts/demo.sh` passes from a fresh clone.\n\n### 8.1 `scripts/demo.sh`\nOwner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: phases 3–7.\n- 8.1.1 Start compose (db, redis, worker, fake), migrate, create the users and tokens, and\n  start the web process.\n- 8.1.2 Run four scenarios with `SALESFORCE_RATE_LIMIT=5`, printing ✅/❌ for each:\n  1. duplicate webhook → one change;\n  2. older event after a newer one → current value kept, history has both;\n  3. a webhook isn't sent back to Salesforce (0 outbox rows, and the fake sees no call);\n  4. fake down → portal edits → worker restarted → fake up → every edit arrives.\n- 8.1.3 Print the measured request rate. It must stay ≤ 5 req/s.\n\n**Done when:** all checks pass twice in a row from a fresh clone.\n\n### 8.2 Outage arithmetic check\nOwner: Ross. Depends on: 8.1.\n- 8.2.1 A scaled-down run: N pending edits at limit L should drain in about N ÷ L s. Compare\n  with the §10 formula.\n\n**Done when:** the measured time is within 10 % of N ÷ L.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 9: Submission\n\n**Goal:** the three required deliverables are complete and consistent.\n**Exit:** the design doc, the chats and the commits match the code.\n\n### 9.1 Design document final pass\nOwner: Chandler → Monica. Depends on: phase 8.\n- 9.1.1 Every section in the brief's outline is filled. No TODO except things explicitly left\n  out (§12).\n- 9.1.2 Every rule in the doc has a test, and every test is in the doc (Monica cross-checks).\n- 9.1.3 The open-questions list, with one \"if the other way\" sentence per assumption.\n\n### 9.2 Walkthrough notes\nOwner: Chandler. Depends on: 9.1.\n- 9.2.1 `docs/walkthrough.md` in the brief's order, about 10 minutes: assumptions and open\n  questions → diagram → rules (conflict, order, loop, outage) → arithmetic.\n\n### 9.3 Chats and commits\nOwner: user (`/ready-to-commit`). Depends on: 9.1.\n- 9.3.1 The final export includes subagent chats (1.1.5).\n- 9.3.2 Every phase ends in a commit whose subject states its decision.\n\n**Done when:** the user has reviewed and committed. Pushing is the user's call.\n\n---\n\n## Tracking\n\n| Phase | Status |\n|---|---|\n| 0 Scaffold | ✅ done |\n| 1 Foundations | ⏳ 1.5 in progress (`openapi.yml` written and validated) |\n| 2 `apply()` | — |\n| 3 Inbound webhook | — |\n| 4 Fake Salesforce | — |\n| 5 Outbound and outage | — |\n| 6 Catch-up | — |\n| 7 Portal API | — |\n| 8 Demo | — |\n| 9 Submission | — |\n"
}

## Claude

The build plan is written, and the Django apps, models and endpoints are decided, with an OpenAPI contract for the endpoints. Nothing is committed. I paused `/ready-to-commit` partway, so nothing was staged; re-run it when you're ready.

## What's decided

**Apps:**
- **`sync`** (it already exists): the customer and contact records, the sync tables, `apply()`, the API views and the background tasks.
- **`fake_salesforce`** (new): the stand-in CRM the brief asks for. It runs as its own process with its own SQLite database, so "Salesforce is down" can be a really stopped container.
- **`utils`**: unchanged.

**Models** (full column list in `design.md` §4):

| Model | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `Customer`, `Contact` | The records. Each keeps our own ID (also sent to Salesforce as its external ID), the Salesforce ID, and per field: when it was last set, by whom, and the last value Salesforce sent |
| `ChangeEvent` | Duplicate detection: the event ID is unique in the database |
| `FieldChange` | The history: who changed what and when, append-only |
| `Outbox` | Edits waiting to go to Salesforce. At most one pending row per record, so repeated edits merge |
| `SyncState` | Catch-up position, and whether Salesforce is up or down |

**Endpoints:** `docs/openapi.yml` (OpenAPI 3.1, checked with a validator: 9 paths, 13 operations). Every one is a DRF generic view:
- the Salesforce webhook;
- list, create, get and edit for customers and for contacts, each with a history endpoint;
- a sync-status endpoint reporting the three numbers to watch;
- the existing `/health/`.

## The plan: `docs/build-plan.md`

It's also published as a **Build Plan** wiki page. It has 9 phases, 25 tasks and about 75 subtasks. Each task has an owner, what it depends on, and a testable "done when". The phases run riskiest-first, and `design.md` §3 now explains why:

1. **Foundations:** fill the team's skill gaps, settings and login, models, Django admin, the contract.
2. **`apply()`:** the riskiest part, because every rule the brief checks runs inside it.
3. **Inbound webhook** (path A).
4. **Fake Salesforce.**
5. **Outbound and outage handling** (path B): the second riskiest.
6. **Catch-up** (path C).
7. **Portal API.**
8. **One-command demo** of the brief's four checks.
9. **Submission.**

**Work keeps going instead of stopping to ask.** The plan has a table of defaults for every open question, and the team rules now say: take the default, record it as an assumption, mark it `DEFAULTED` in the task file, and carry on. Agents stop only if the next step would:
- contradict the brief;
- reverse a decision you made;
- do something irreversible or outside this machine (deleting data, rewriting history, pushing);
- weaken security.

**Defaults you should review:**
- **Portal login (Q14):** each portal user gets a DRF token, the same mechanism as the webhook. It's in `design.md` as an assumption.
- **The three review findings from earlier:**
  - "which fields changed" is worked out inside the record lock;
  - echo detection is done field by field;
  - catch-up's record-level timestamps are accepted as a known limit.

**Also fixed:** stale text the docs agent found in the agent files, the compose file and the skill example. Tests pass (7), and the wiki builds (7 pages).

**Next:** task 1.1, filling the team's skill gaps (sync-engine, fake-Salesforce and testing skills, and exporting the subagents' chats). I'll do that myself, because it changes the team. From task 1.2 on, it's `/monica <task>`. Say go and I'll start 1.1.

## Claude

They line up today with one exception, and that exception proves your point. `1.5.0` ("openapi.yml written") is in `task.todo` but not in the plan, because I added it to the board and forgot the plan. That's exactly the drift a manual setup lets through.

## How the two files relate now

| | `docs/build-plan.md` | `task.todo` |
|---|---|---|
| Holds | **What** each task is: goal, owner, dependencies, subtasks, "done when" | **Where we are**: ☐ / ✔ / ✘ per ID |
| Link between them | — | Same IDs (`1.2.3`), plus a header line pointing to the plan |
| If you edit the plan | — | **Nothing happens.** `task.todo` doesn't change. |

Keeping them in step depends only on the rules: wording changes go through the plan first, and Chandler checks for drift after each task. That catches mistakes late, if at all.

## The fix I'd suggest: generate `task.todo` from the plan

A small script, `scripts/sync-todo.py`:
- **Rebuild:** it reads the phases, tasks and subtasks from `build-plan.md` and writes `task.todo`.
- **Statuses survive:** for each ID it keeps the existing ✔ / ✘ / `@started` / `@done` / `@defaulted` from the current `task.todo`.
- **New, renamed, removed tasks:**
  - a task new to the plan appears as ☐;
  - a reworded task gets the new wording and keeps its status;
  - a task removed from the plan is listed under "Removed from plan" instead of silently disappearing. A ✔ item is never lost.
- **`--check` mode:** exits with an error if the two disagree. I'd run it as a test and in `/ready-to-commit` step b, so drift can't get committed.

Then the workflow becomes:
- **Change a task** → edit `build-plan.md`, then run `python3 scripts/sync-todo.py`.
- **Change a status** → edit `task.todo` directly, or Monica does it. The script never touches statuses.

It's about 60 lines plus a test. It would also fix the `1.5.0` drift: I'd add that subtask to the plan, where it belongs. Should I build it?

## User

why do we need fake_salesforce django app? is this for testing purpose?

## Claude

Yes. It's for **testing and the demo only**. It never ships, and in real use the worker talks to real Salesforce. But the brief more or less requires it. Here's why.

## Why we need a fake at all

The brief says so directly:
- *"Out of scope for this weekend: … a load test against real Salesforce. **If you write a program, call a fake CRM you write yourself.**"*
- One of the four checks it lists: *"a pending call that is still there after a restart **while the fake Salesforce is down**."*
- *"In a demo you may set a lower cap so the wait is visible. The code must enforce the cap it is given."*

We also don't have a Salesforce account. Even if we did, we couldn't make it go down for 6 hours, return 429s, or reject a record on demand. The fake lets us cause every failure the design handles, whenever we want.

## Why a separate running service, and not just a mock in the tests

There are two levels of fake in the plan, for different jobs:

| | In-test fake (plan 5.1.3) | Fake Salesforce service (phase 4) |
|---|---|---|
| What | A Python class that stands in for `SalesforceClient` inside the tests | A small separate service in docker compose, reached over real HTTP |
| Used for | Fast unit tests: retries, backoff, mapping each response to an outcome | End-to-end tests and the demo |
| Can it really go "down"? | Only pretend | **Yes:** `docker compose stop fake-salesforce` |
| Sends webhooks to us? | No | **Yes:** sales edits, duplicates, older-after-newer, and our own updates echoed back |
| Keeps records? | No | **Yes:** upsert by external ID, "changed since" queries for catch-up |

Three of the brief's checks need the second kind. The duplicate and out-of-order checks need something that actually *sends* webhooks. The sync-loop check needs something that echoes our update back as a webhook. And the restart-while-down check needs something that's actually unreachable. A mock inside a test can't stop being reachable while the worker restarts.

## Why build it as a Django app

It doesn't have to be. The alternatives:

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **Django app** (planned) | Same image, same stack, same rules and tests; its own small database stands in for "Salesforce has its own database" | A bit heavier than a script |
| A standalone Python script (stdlib only) | Tiny, nothing to install | We'd hand-write its HTTP handling, data storage and webhook sending, and it's outside our test setup |
| A mock server generated from an API spec | No code to write | Can't remember records or send webhooks, so it can't do catch-up, echoes or the outage check |

I picked a Django app because the team already knows the stack and its rules cover it. It runs from the same Docker image as its own process, and it's **never added to the portal's installed apps**, so none of it ships with the portal. If you'd rather have something lighter, a single-file stdlib server works too; it's just more hand-written code for the same behaviour.

Do you want to keep the Django app, or switch to a standalone script?

1. **`apply()` comes first (phase 2).** Every rule the brief checks runs inside it: duplicate,
   out-of-order, sync loop, history. If it's wrong, nothing built on top can be right, and it
   needs no network, so it's the cheapest place to prove the rules.
2. **Outbound and outage come next (phases 4–5).** This is where data gets lost if we're wrong:
   the 6-hour outage, retries counted in the cap, surviving restarts. Building the fake

3. **Catch-up (phase 6)** depends on both of the above. **The portal API (phase 7)** is a thin
## Phase 4: Fake Salesforce

**Goal:** a separate process that behaves like the parts of Salesforce we depend on, and that
can be broken on demand.
**Exit:** the fake runs in compose, and each mode is tested.

### 4.1 The fake app and its process
Owner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 1.1.2.
- 4.1.1 `fake_salesforce` app with its own settings module and SQLite database.
- 4.1.2 A compose service `fake-salesforce` (same image) on port 8001.
- 4.1.3 Record API: upsert by external ID, update by ID, and a "changed since T" query paged at
  2,000 records (Q3, Q13). Token-checked.

**Done when:** an upsert twice with the same external ID gives one record, and the query pages
correctly.

### 4.2 Failure modes
Owner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 4.1.
- 4.2.1 Control endpoint: `up`, `slow` (delay), `throttle` (429 with `Retry-After`), `error`
  (5xx), `reject` (400 for a given record).
- 4.2.2 "Down" is a stopped container: `docker compose stop fake-salesforce`.

**Done when:** each mode returns the documented response.

### 4.3 Webhook sender
Owner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 4.1, 3.1.
- 4.3.1 A record change in the fake (a "sales edit" via its control endpoint, or our API write)
  sends a whole-record webhook to the portal with `eventId`, `occurredAt` and `changedBy`. Our
  own writes are sent with `changedBy` = the integration user (the echo).
- 4.3.2 A control option to send the same webhook twice, or an older one after a newer one.

**Done when:** a sales edit in the fake appears in the portal within 30 s.

---

## Phase 5: Outbound (path B) and the outage

**Goal:** portal edits reach Salesforce under the cap, and survive outages and restarts.
**Exit:** a restart while the fake is down loses nothing, and the measured rate never exceeds
the configured cap.

### 5.1 `SalesforceClient`
Owner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 1.2, 4.1.
- 5.1.1 An `httpx` client: `upsert(object_type, external_id, fields)` and `update(...)`.
- 5.1.2 Maps responses to outcomes: ok, unreachable, throttled (with `Retry-After`), rejected,
  auth failure.
- 5.1.3 An in-process fake for unit tests, with the same outcomes.

**Done when:** each outcome is mapped correctly against the in-process fake.

### 5.2 Shared rate limiter
Owner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 5.1.
- 5.2.1 A Redis token bucket (Lua, atomic) at `SALESFORCE_RATE_LIMIT`, shared by every worker
  thread and process, and used for sends, retries, probes and catch-up queries.
- 5.2.2 On a 429: pause until `Retry-After`, halve the rate, then add 5 req/s every 30 s back
  up to the limit.

**Done when:** with the limit at 5 req/s and an injected clock, 100 calls take ≥ 19 s (no
window exceeds the limit); a 429 halves the rate.

### 5.3 Outbound task
Owner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 5.2, 2.3.
- 5.3.1 A Dramatiq actor with `max_retries=0` that claims due rows (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`,
  `lease_until`), reads the record's **current** values for the fields, and sends.
- 5.3.2 Outcome handling per design §6: `sent` and store the Salesforce ID; backoff
  1/2/4/8… s capped at 60 s; 429 → slow the limiter down; 400 → `needs_review`; 401/403 →
  stop and alert.
- 5.3.3 Wake-up: a Redis nudge on commit (`transaction.on_commit`), plus a 5-second crontab
  sweep.

**Done when:**
- a portal edit is in the fake within 30 s;
- a 5xx is retried and then sent;
- a 400 goes to `needs_review` and is never dropped;
- a worker killed mid-call loses its lease and the row is sent again.

### 5.4 Down detection and probe
Owner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: 5.3.
- 5.4.1 After 5 consecutive unreachable failures, `SyncState` says `down` and sending stops.
- 5.4.2 A probe every 10 s. On success: `up`, trigger catch-up (phase 6), then make every
  pending row due.

**Done when:** with the fake stopped, the state goes `down` after 5 failures; with it
restarted, it goes `up` within 10 s and the drain starts.

### 5.5 Restart-while-down test (brief check)
Owner: Ross. Depends on: 5.4.
- 5.5.1 Stop the fake, make portal edits, restart the worker container, start the fake again,
  and check every edit arrives in the fake.

**Done when:** that test passes. This is one of the brief's four demo checks.

---

## Phase 8: Demo and end-to-end check

**Goal:** one command from a fresh checkout shows the brief's four checks, with a cap low
enough to see.
**Exit:** `bash scripts/demo.sh` passes from a fresh clone.

### 8.1 `scripts/demo.sh`
Owner: Phoebe → Ross. Depends on: phases 3–7.
- 8.1.1 Start compose (db, redis, worker, fake), migrate, create the users and tokens, and
  start the web process.
- 8.1.2 Run four scenarios with `SALESFORCE_RATE_LIMIT=5`, printing ✅/❌ for each:
  1. duplicate webhook → one change;
  2. older event after a newer one → current value kept, history has both;
  3. a webhook isn't sent back to Salesforce (0 outbox rows, and the fake sees no call);
  4. fake down → portal edits → worker restarted → fake up → every edit arrives.
- 8.1.3 Print the measured request rate. It must stay ≤ 5 req/s.

**Done when:** all checks pass twice in a row from a fresh clone.

### 8.2 Outage arithmetic check
Owner: Ross. Depends on: 8.1.
- 8.2.1 A scaled-down run: N pending edits at limit L should drain in about N ÷ L s. Compare
  with the §10 formula.

**Done when:** the measured time is within 10 % of N ÷ L.

---

## Claude

The separate fake-Salesforce app is gone from the plan. Salesforce is now faked inside the test suite, so there's no extra app or container. Nothing is built or committed yet; this was a plan change.

**What replaces the app (phase 4, "Test scenarios"):**

| Piece | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `FakeSalesforce` | `src/sync/tests/fakes.py` | Keeps records in memory, handles upsert by external ID and the "changed since" query, and can be switched to down, slow, 429, 5xx, rejected or bad-login. Its call log lets tests check what was sent and how fast. |
| Plug-in point | `httpx.MockTransport` | Tests run our real `SalesforceClient` code against the fake, with no network. It's built into httpx, so no new dependency. |
| Local server fixture | stdlib HTTP server | Only for the restart test, which needs a real separate worker process |
| Scenario builders | `src/sync/tests/scenarios.py` | A sales edit as a whole-record webhook, a duplicate, an older event after a newer one, and our own update coming back |

**The brief's four checks are still covered,** as tests marked `brief`:
1. **Duplicate webhook:** the same payload posted twice gives one change.
2. **Older event after a newer one:** the newer value stays current, and both are in the history.
3. **No echo back to Salesforce:** a webhook creates no outbox row, and the fake receives no call.
4. **Restart while Salesforce is down:**
   - the fake is set to down, and portal edits are made;
   - the worker process is killed and a new one started;
   - the fake is set back to up;
   - every edit arrives.

The demo is still one command, `bash scripts/demo.sh`. It starts Postgres and Redis, then runs those four tests at a 5 req/s cap, printing ✅ or ❌ for each and the request rate measured from the fake's call log.

**Updated to match:**
- `build-plan.md`:
  - phase 4 is rewritten;
  - 5.1.3, 5.4, 5.5 and phase 8 now use the in-test fake;
  - the apps table no longer has `fake_salesforce`;
  - skill 1.1.2 is now `sync-test-scenarios`.
- `task.todo`: the same items.
- `design.md` §3, the `openapi.yml` description and the wiki's Development Workflow page.

`openapi.yml` still validates, and the wiki builds. No references to a fake app remain anywhere.

`task.todo` is deleted. `docs/build-plan.md` is now the single file: the plan and its checklist. Nothing is committed.

**How the checklist works:**
- **Every subtask is a checkbox.** 73 subtasks were converted. The plan gained 1.5.0 (`openapi.yml`), which was only on the old board, so that drift is gone. 3 items are ticked (1.1.4, 1.5.0, 1.5.2) and 71 are open.

## Acceptance criteria
<!-- Joey drafts; Monica approves. Each one testable. Cite the brief or design section. -->

Source key: BP = `docs/build-plan.md`, D = `docs/design.md`, API = `docs/openapi.yml`, R = `.claude/rules/drf.md`.
Commands below are run from the repo root with compose services up. Never print `.env` values.

**1.2 Settings and authentication** (Slice A)

- **AC-1.2.1** `rest_framework.authtoken` is in `INSTALLED_APPS` (`src/config/settings.py`) and
  its migration applies: `Token` rows can be created, and `manage.py migrate` on an empty DB
  succeeds. (BP 1.2.1)
- **AC-1.2.2** `REST_FRAMEWORK` in `src/config/settings.py` sets `DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES`
  to `TokenAuthentication` only and `DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES` to `IsAuthenticated`. Test: a
  request to a protected URL with no token gets 401 (not 403), and with a bad token gets 401.
  `HealthView` (`src/utils/views.py`) declares `permission_classes = [AllowAny]` explicitly (and
  needs no auth, so `GET /api/v1/health/` is 200 without a token). (BP 1.2.2, R "Authentication
  and permissions", D Q14) `DEFAULTED` Q14: DRF token per portal user.
  Note for Ross: no protected view exists yet, so the 401 test may use a throwaway view or
  `override_settings`/`APIRequestFactory`; do not add a real endpoint for it (don't build ahead).
- **AC-1.2.3** Integration user: a group named exactly `salesforce-integration`; permission class
  `IsSalesforceIntegration` (in `src/sync/permissions.py`) that allows only an authenticated user
  in that group (a portal user without the group is denied, anonymous is denied); management
  command `src/sync/management/commands/create_integration_user.py` (with `__init__.py` files)
  that creates the group and user if missing, creates the token, and prints it once. Re-running
  must not crash and must not create a second user. Tests: permission class allow/deny for the
  three cases; command run via `call_command` creates exactly one user in the group with one
  token and the printed token equals `Token.objects.get(...).key`. (BP 1.2.3, D Q11, R)
- **AC-1.2.4** `httpx` is a dependency in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` (added with `uv add`,
  importable). `src/config/settings.py` reads `SALESFORCE_BASE_URL`, `SALESFORCE_TOKEN` and
  `SALESFORCE_RATE_LIMIT` (int, default 90) through django-environ. `.env` and `.env.example`
  contain the same set of keys: test or command compares key names only (never values), e.g.
  parse both files for `KEY=` names and assert set equality. (BP 1.2.4, D Q10)

**1.3 Models and migrations** (Slice A). All in `src/sync/models.py`, migrations in
`src/sync/migrations/`, column layout per D §4 and the lengths in API.

- **AC-1.3.1** `Customer`: `external_id` UUID (default uuid4, unique), `salesforce_id`
  varchar(18) unique and nullable, `name` (255), `status` (40), `owner` (255), `field_meta`
  JSONField (default dict), `created_at`, `updated_at`. `Contact`: same sync columns plus
  `full_name` (255), `phone` (40), `email` (254, indexed), `city` (120), `owner` (255),
  `customer` FK to `Customer`, `null=True`, `on_delete=PROTECT`, indexed, and
  `customer_salesforce_id` varchar(18), indexed (blank default). Test: deleting a customer that
  has a contact raises `ProtectedError`; two customers with `salesforce_id=None` coexist, two
  with the same non-null `salesforce_id` raise `IntegrityError`; a duplicate `external_id`
  raises `IntegrityError` for both models. (BP 1.3.1, D §4)
  `DEFAULTED`: contact with an unknown customer stores `customer_salesforce_id`, FK null (BP
  Defaults).
- **AC-1.3.2** `ChangeEvent`: `event_id` varchar(128) with a **database-level** unique
  constraint, `source`, `received_at` (indexed). `FieldChange`: `object_type`, `record_id`,
  `field`, `value` (text, null), `actor`, `source`, `occurred_at`, `status` with choices
  `applied`/`superseded`/`echo`, `event_id`, `created_at`. `Outbox`: `object_type`, `record_id`,
  `operation` (`create`/`update`), `fields` (array of strings, `ArrayField` or JSON list, as
  D §4 says "array"), `state` (`pending`/`sent`/`needs_review`, default `pending`), `attempts`
  (default 0), `next_attempt_at`, `lease_until` (null), `last_error`, `created_at`, `sent_at`
  (null). `SyncState`: `key` primary key, `value` JSONField, `updated_at`. Test: a duplicate
  `event_id` raises `IntegrityError` (use `transaction.atomic` and the real DB, not a mock).
  (BP 1.3.2, D §4, §8)
- **AC-1.3.3** Outbox has a **partial unique constraint** on `(object_type, record_id)` with
  `condition=Q(state="pending")`: a second `pending` row for the same record raises
  `IntegrityError`, but a `sent` or `needs_review` row plus one `pending` row for the same
  record is allowed, and `pending` rows for different records or object types are allowed.
  Test checks it at database level and also inspects `pg_indexes`/`Meta.constraints`. Outbox has
  an index on `(state, next_attempt_at)`; `FieldChange` has an index on
  `(object_type, record_id, occurred_at)`; `ChangeEvent.received_at` is indexed; Contact has
  indexes on `customer`, `customer_salesforce_id`, `email`. Test queries `pg_indexes` (or
  `connection.introspection.get_constraints`) for each. All indexes ship in the same migration
  as their model. (BP 1.3.3, D §4, R "Models and migrations")
- **AC-1.3.4** Model tests live in `src/sync/tests/test_models.py` and cover AC-1.3.1 to
  AC-1.3.3 against real Postgres. The old `src/sync/tests.py` file is removed so `src/sync/tests/`
  (with `__init__.py`) is a package (BP 4.1.1 uses `src/sync/tests/`). Migrations apply on an
  empty database; `uv run python src/manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` prints "No
  changes detected" and exits 0. Times are timezone-aware (`USE_TZ`). (BP 1.3.4, R)

**1.4 Django admin** (Slice B). All in `src/sync/admin.py`; tests in
`src/sync/tests/test_admin.py`.

- **AC-1.4.1** `Customer` and `Contact` are registered with `list_display`, `search_fields`
  limited to indexed columns (Customer: `external_id`, `salesforce_id`; Contact: `email`,
  `salesforce_id`, `customer_salesforce_id`, `external_id`; never `name` or `city`),
  `list_select_related` (Contact: `("customer",)`), `ordering`, `show_full_result_count = False`,
  and `raw_id_fields = ("customer",)` on Contact. Tests as a superuser: each changelist,
  add page, change page and a search query return 200; the Contact change page contains no
  `<select` for customer (raw id widget instead); `list_select_related` produces a fixed query
  count for a changelist with several contacts (`django_assert_num_queries` or
  `CaptureQueriesContext`, no N+1). (BP 1.4.1, R "Django admin")
- **AC-1.4.2** `FieldChange` and `ChangeEvent` are registered and read-only:
  `has_add_permission`, `has_change_permission` and `has_delete_permission` all return `False`
  (checked for a superuser). Tests: the add URL returns 403, a POST to the change URL and to
  the delete URL does not alter or remove the row, and the changelist still returns 200 with
  `list_display`, `ordering`, `show_full_result_count = False`. (BP 1.4.2, R)
- **AC-1.4.3** `Outbox` and `SyncState` are registered. `Outbox` is read-only (no add, change,
  delete; add URL 403) and has an admin action `requeue` that only touches rows with
  `state="needs_review"`: they become `pending` with `next_attempt_at` set to now, `attempts`
  reset to 0 and `lease_until` cleared; rows in other states are untouched (test with one
  `needs_review`, one `sent`, one `pending` selected together). The action must not create a
  second pending row for a record that already has one (the partial unique constraint must not
  surface as a 500: skip or report it). Every model is registered: Customer, Contact,
  ChangeEvent, FieldChange, Outbox, SyncState each have a changelist that returns 200.
  (BP 1.4.3, D §6 "needs_review", Q9, R)
  `DEFAULTED`: requeue-collision behaviour (skip with a message) because the brief and D §6 do
  not say.

**1.6 URL layout and serializers** (Slice B)

- **AC-1.6.1** `src/config/urls.py` has `path("api/v1/", include(...))` exactly once, with
  `utils.urls` first and `sync.urls` second, plus `admin/`. The string `api/v1` appears in no
  other file under `src/` (grep test, excluding `tests/`). The old root `health/` route is gone.
  (BP 1.6.1, R "Layout and URLs", user decision)
- **AC-1.6.2** `src/utils/urls.py` has `app_name = "utils"` and one route named `health`
  (`reverse("utils:health")` == `/api/v1/health/`); `src/sync/urls.py` has `app_name = "sync"` and
  an empty `urlpatterns` with a comment listing the planned routes from BP "Endpoints". Neither
  file contains `api/v1`. (BP 1.6.2, R)
- **AC-1.6.3** `src/utils/serializers.py` holds `HealthSerializer` (removed from
  `src/utils/views.py`, which imports it). `src/sync/serializers.py` holds `CustomerSerializer`,
  `ContactSerializer` and `FieldChangeSerializer`, each with explicit `fields` (no `"__all__"`),
  `read_only_fields` covering the server-owned fields (`id`, `external_id`, `salesforce_id`,
  `sync_state`/`updated_at` as applicable), and field names as in API. API uses camelCase
  (`fullName`, `externalId`, `salesforceId`, `updatedAt`, `eventId`, `occurredAt`); BP 7.1.1
  assigns camelCase to phase 7, so for phase 1 the criterion is: field set equals the API
  property set for each schema, with camelCase output names. `DEFAULTED`: render camelCase now
  with explicit `source=` mapping on each field (no new dependency) because API is the contract
  and re-keying later would break tests. Contact `customer` is the portal ID (integer). Do not
  add `sync_state` unless it can be computed without a query per row; if it cannot, leave it out
  and record it as a gap in the ledger for phase 7 (Phoebe decides, Monica checks). Serializers
  must not call `.save()` anywhere (writes go through `apply()` in phase 2; R). (BP 1.6.3, R, API)
- **AC-1.6.4** Tests (`src/utils/tests/test_health.py` updated, `src/sync/tests/test_serializers.py`
  and `src/sync/tests/test_urls.py` new): `GET /api/v1/health/` is 200 with `postgres` and
  `redis` keys; `GET /health/` is 404; `reverse("utils:health")` resolves; every named route in
  the two `urls.py` files reverses; serializer field lists equal the API property sets and each
  server-owned field is read-only (assert via `serializer.fields[name].read_only`). (BP 1.6.4)

- Each app has its own `urls.py` (with `app_name`) and `serializers.py`.
- `reverse("utils:health")` gives `/api/v1/health/`. The `sync` app's `urls.py` is empty for now, with a comment listing the routes planned for phases 3 and 7.

**Six models** with real database constraints, all confirmed in the live database:
- `Customer` and `Contact`;
- `ChangeEvent`, with a unique event ID (duplicate detection);
- `FieldChange`, the history;
- `Outbox`, with the rule that each record can have at most one `pending` row;
- `SyncState`.

**Also built:**
- DRF token auth, as the default.
- A permission class and a `create_integration_user` command for the Salesforce webhook. Run `uv run python src/manage.py create_integration_user` to get its token.
- `httpx`, plus the Salesforce settings in `.env` and `.env.example`.
- The Django admin for all six models: the history and dedupe tables are read-only, and the outbox has a "requeue failed rows" action.

## Claude

**No, not as a column.** There is no `created_by` or `updated_by` on `Customer` or `Contact`.

**What we do save, and where:**

| Who changed it | Where it's recorded |
|---|---|
| Who changed **each field**, and when | `FieldChange.actor` and `occurred_at`, one row per change. It's written for every edit, including superseded ones. The brief asks for exactly this: *"who changed the phone, and who changed the city"*. |
| Who made the **current** value of each field | `field_meta` on the record: per field `by`, `at` and `source`. Design §4 specifies it. |
| When the record was created or last touched | `created_at` and `updated_at` on every record |
| **Who created the record** | **Nowhere as its own field.** The record's first `FieldChange` rows have the actor, but you'd have to look it up. |

I'd say that's the right shape: "who created it" is really "who set the first value", and the brief wants history per field. But it's not saved as `created_by`.

**Gaps I see:**
1. **The record's own creator** isn't a direct column, so the admin and the API can't show it without a lookup.
2. **`field_meta.by` isn't filled in yet.** It's a JSON column that phase 2's `apply()` will write. Right now nothing records any actor, because no write path exists yet.
3. **Salesforce-created records:** the actor would be the webhook's `changedBy`, a Salesforce user ID or email, not a portal user.

**Options:**
- **(A) Leave it as is.** `FieldChange` is the audit trail, and a creator is its first rows.
- **(B) Add `created_by` and `updated_by`** to `Customer` and `Contact`: two nullable text columns, set by `apply()`. They're cheap, show in the admin and API, and answer "who created this" directly.
- **(C) Also expose them in the API** (`createdBy`, `updatedBy`) alongside `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.

I'd go with **(B)**, plus (C) if you want it in the API. Is that what you were asking about? Which do you want? If B, it's a small change to the models, one migration, and `apply()` fills them in when we build phase 2.

import uuid

from django.contrib.postgres.fields import ArrayField
from django.db import models
from django.db.models import Q


class SyncRecord(models.Model):
    """Columns shared by every record synced with Salesforce (design §4)."""

    external_id = models.UUIDField(default=uuid.uuid4, unique=True)
    salesforce_id = models.CharField(max_length=18, unique=True, null=True, blank=True)
    field_meta = models.JSONField(default=dict, blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        abstract = True


class Customer(SyncRecord):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=40)
    owner = models.CharField(max_length=255)


class Contact(SyncRecord):
    full_name = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    phone = models.CharField(max_length=40)
    email = models.EmailField(max_length=254, db_index=True)
    city = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    owner = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    customer = models.ForeignKey(Customer, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="contacts")
    customer_salesforce_id = models.CharField(max_length=18, db_index=True, blank=True, default="")


class ChangeEvent(models.Model):
    event_id = models.CharField(max_length=128)
    source = models.CharField(max_length=40)
    received_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, db_index=True)

## Claude

Both options are in progress, and I've handled the contract first, as before.

**What's decided:**
- **B:** `Customer` and `Contact` get `created_by` and `updated_by`. They're text columns (up to 255 characters, empty by default), added to the shared base so both models get them, with one new migration. They're empty until phase 2's `apply()` fills them: it will set `created_by` when a record is created and `updated_by` on every change.
- **C:** the API returns `createdAt`, `createdBy`, `updatedAt` and `updatedBy` on customers and contacts, all read-only. The Django admin shows them read-only too.
- **Docstrings:** every model class gets a docstring saying what it's for, its constraints and indexes by their real names, and which design section describes it.
